title: Wonder Facts
intro: A few quiet facts, just for wonder. They are the kind that stay true.

cards.back: Honey is very low in water and slightly acidic, so sealed honey can stay good for a very long time.
Two hearts pump blood through the gills, and one sends it around the rest of the body.

cards.front: A day on Venus is long
cards.back: Venus spins so slowly that one full turn takes about 243 Earth days, longer than its 225-day trip around the Sun.

cards.front: Bananas are berries, strawberries are not
cards.back: Botanists call a fruit a berry by how it grows. By that rule, bananas count and strawberries do not.
Fungal threads wrap around many tree roots and help them take up water and nutrients. In return the tree feeds the fungi sugars.

cards.front: Light takes a while to reach us
cards.back: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to travel from the Sun to the Earth.

cards.front: Sound needs something to travel through
cards.back: In space there is almost no air, so sound has nothing to carry it.
Wombats make small cubes, which stay put on rocks and logs instead of rolling away.

cards.front: The Moon is slowly drifting away
cards.back: It moves away from Earth by a few centimetres every year.
From the ground we usually see an arc, but from high up, such as an aircraft, a full circle can appear.
Bone is living tissue. It is slowly rebuilt over the years, and it can mend itself.
A returning bee can wiggle in a pattern that tells nestmates which way, and roughly how far, to find flowers.
